interconnectors.name: Eastern Green Link 1 (Torness to Hawthorn Pit)

ai_summary:
Scotland's renewable energy sector is demonstrating exceptional operational momentum, with wind generation reaching an impressive 4.4 GW. This robust surge in zero-carbon supply has driven regional carbon intensity down to an ultra-low 32 gCO2/kWh, underscoring Scotland’s role as the primary engine of Great Britain’s clean energy transition. The grid is operating with remarkable carbon efficiency, displacing fossil-fuel baseload across the wider national network.

However, this substantial volume continues to expose structural transmission constraints, evidenced by 221.1 MWh of wasted energy logged through curtailment actions. Export limitations across the Anglo-Scottish boundary prevent the full evacuation of clean electricity to southern demand centers. Consequently, the system operator must rely on costly constraint payments to turn down Scottish turbines while balancing the wider grid with localized generation elsewhere.

To eliminate these efficiency losses, industry stakeholders and network planners must expedite high-voltage direct current transmission upgrades and incentivize co-located battery energy storage installations. Expanding regional demand-side response mechanisms and green hydrogen production could also effectively absorb this 221.1 MWh of stranded power, ensuring peak wind output translates into sustained commercial and environmental value.
